NASB.1: 'Behold, my eye has seen all [this], My ear has heard and understood it.
NASB.2: 'What you know I also know; I am not inferior to you.
NASB.3: 'But I would speak to the Almighty, And I desire to argue with God.
NASB.4: 'But you smear with lies; You are all worthless physicians.
NASB.5: 'O that you would be completely silent, And that it would become your wisdom!
NASB.6: 'Please hear my argument And listen to the contentions of my lips.
NASB.7: 'Will you speak what is unjust for God, And speak what is deceitful for Him?
NASB.8: 'Will you show partiality for Him? Will you contend for God?
NASB.9: 'Will it be well when He examines you? Or will you deceive Him as one deceives a man?
NASB.10: 'He will surely reprove you If you secretly show partiality.
NASB.11: 'Will not His majesty terrify you, And the dread of Him fall on you?
NASB.12: 'Your memorable sayings are proverbs of ashes, Your defenses are defenses of clay.
NASB.13: 'Be silent before me so that I may speak; Then let come on me what may.
NASB.14: 'Why should I take my flesh in my teeth And put my life in my hands?
NASB.15: 'Though He slay me, I will hope in Him. Nevertheless I will argue my ways before Him.
NASB.16: 'This also will be my salvation, For a godless man may not come before His presence.
NASB.17: 'Listen carefully to my speech, And let my declaration [fill] your ears.

NASB.19: 'Who will contend with me? For then I would be silent and die.
NASB.20: 'Only two things do not do to me, Then I will not hide from Your face:

NASB.22: 'Then call, and I will answer; Or let me speak, then reply to me.
NASB.23: 'How many are my iniquities and sins? Make known to me my rebellion and my sin.
NASB.24: 'Why do You hide Your face And consider me Your enemy?
NASB.25: 'Will You cause a driven leaf to tremble? Or will You pursue the dry chaff?

AMP.1:
[Job continued:] "Behold, my eye has seen all this,
My ear has heard and understood it.
AMP.2:
"What you know I also know;
I am not inferior to you.
AMP.3:
"But I wish to speak to the Almighty,
And I desire to argue with God.
AMP.4:
"But you smear me with lies [you defame my character most untruthfully];
You are all worthless physicians and have no remedy to offer.
AMP.5:
"Oh, that you would be completely silent,
And that silence would be your wisdom!
AMP.6:
"Please hear my argument
And listen to the pleadings of my lips.
AMP.7:
"Will you speak what is unjust for God,
And speak what is deceitful for Him?
AMP.8:
"Will you show partiality for Him [and be unjust to me so that you may gain favor with Him]?
Will you contend and plead for God?
AMP.9:
"Will it be well for you when He investigates you [and your tactics against me]?
Or will you deceive Him as one deceives a man?
AMP.10:
"He will surely reprimand you
If you secretly show partiality.
AMP.11:
"Will not His majesty terrify you,
And will not the dread of Him fall upon you?
AMP.12:
"Your memorable sayings are [worthless, merely] proverbs of ashes;
Your defenses are defenses of [crumbling] clay.
AMP.13:
"Be silent before me so that I may speak;
And let happen to me what may.
AMP.14:
"Why should I take my flesh in my teeth
And put my life in my hands [incurring the wrath of God]?
AMP.15:
"Even though He kills me;
I will hope in Him.
Nevertheless, I will argue my ways to His face.
AMP.16:
"This also will be my salvation,
For a godless man may not come before Him.
AMP.17:
"Listen diligently to my speech,
And let my declaration fill your ears.
AMP.18:
"Behold now, I have prepared my case;
I know that I will be vindicated.
AMP.19:
"Who will argue and contend with me?
For then I would be silent and die.
AMP.20:
"Only [O Lord,] do not do two things to me,
And then I will not hide myself from Your face:
AMP.21:
Withdraw Your hand from me and remove this bodily suffering,
And let not the dread of You terrify me.
AMP.22:
"Then [Lord,] call, and I will answer;
Or let me speak, and then reply to me.
AMP.23:
"How many are my iniquities and sins [that so much sorrow should come to me]?
Make me recognize and understand my transgression and my sin.
AMP.24:
"Why do You hide Your face [as if offended]
And consider me Your enemy?
AMP.25:
"Will You cause a windblown leaf to tremble?
Will You pursue the chaff of the dry stubble?
AMP.26:
"For You write bitter things against me [in Your indictment]
And make me inherit and suffer for the iniquities of my youth.
AMP.27:
"You also put my feet in the stocks [as punishment]
And [critically] observe all my paths;
You set a circle and limit around the soles of my feet [which I must not overstep],
AMP.28:
While I waste away like a rotten thing,
Like a garment that is moth-eaten.

NLT.1:
“Look, I have seen all this with my own eyes
and heard it with my own ears, and now I understand.
NLT.2:
I know as much as you do.
You are no better than I am.
NLT.3:
As for me, I would speak directly to the Almighty.
I want to argue my case with God himself.
NLT.4:
As for you, you smear me with lies.
As physicians, you are worthless quacks.
NLT.5:
If only you could be silent!
That’s the wisest thing you could do.
NLT.6:
Listen to my charge;
pay attention to my arguments.
NLT.7:
“Are you defending God with lies?
Do you make your dishonest arguments for his sake?
NLT.8:
Will you slant your testimony in his favor?
Will you argue God’s case for him?
NLT.9:
What will happen when he finds out what you are doing?
Can you fool him as easily as you fool people?
NLT.10:
No, you will be in trouble with him
if you secretly slant your testimony in his favor.
NLT.11:
Doesn’t his majesty terrify you?
Doesn’t your fear of him overwhelm you?
NLT.12:
Your platitudes are as valuable as ashes.
Your defense is as fragile as a clay pot.
NLT.13:
“Be silent now and leave me alone.
Let me speak, and I will face the consequences.
NLT.14:
Why should I put myself in mortal danger
and take my life in my own hands?
NLT.15:
God might kill me, but I have no other hope.
I am going to argue my case with him.
NLT.16:
But this is what will save me — I am not godless.
If I were, I could not stand before him.
NLT.17:
“Listen closely to what I am about to say.
Hear me out.
NLT.18:
I have prepared my case;
I will be proved innocent.
NLT.19:
Who can argue with me over this?
And if you prove me wrong, I will remain silent and die.
NLT.20:
“O God, grant me these two things,
and then I will be able to face you.
NLT.21:
Remove your heavy hand from me,
and don’t terrify me with your awesome presence.
NLT.22:
Now summon me, and I will answer!
Or let me speak to you, and you reply.
NLT.23:
Tell me, what have I done wrong?
Show me my rebellion and my sin.
NLT.24:
Why do you turn away from me?
Why do you treat me as your enemy?
NLT.25:
Would you terrify a leaf blown by the wind?
Would you chase dry straw?
NLT.26:
“You write bitter accusations against me
and bring up all the sins of my youth.
NLT.27:
You put my feet in stocks.
You examine all my paths.
You trace all my footprints.
NLT.28:
I waste away like rotting wood,
like a moth-eaten coat.

NRSVCE.4:
As for you, you whitewash with lies;
all of you are worthless physicians.
NRSVCE.5:
If you would only keep silent,
that would be your wisdom!
NRSVCE.6:
Hear now my reasoning,
and listen to the pleadings of my lips.
NRSVCE.7:
Will you speak falsely for God,
and speak deceitfully for him?
NRSVCE.8:
Will you show partiality toward him,
will you plead the case for God?
NRSVCE.9:
Will it be well with you when he searches you out?
Or can you deceive him, as one person deceives another?
NRSVCE.10:
He will surely rebuke you
if in secret you show partiality.
NRSVCE.11:
Will not his majesty terrify you,
and the dread of him fall upon you?
NRSVCE.12:
Your maxims are proverbs of ashes,
your defenses are defenses of clay.
NRSVCE.13:
“Let me have silence, and I will speak,
and let come on me what may.
NRSVCE.14:
I will take my flesh in my teeth,
and put my life in my hand.
NRSVCE.15:
See, he will kill me; I have no hope;
but I will defend my ways to his face.
NRSVCE.16:
This will be my salvation,
that the godless shall not come before him.
NRSVCE.17:
Listen carefully to my words,
and let my declaration be in your ears.
NRSVCE.18:
I have indeed prepared my case;
I know that I shall be vindicated.
NRSVCE.19:
Who is there that will contend with me?
For then I would be silent and die.
NRSVCE.20:
Only grant two things to me,
then I will not hide myself from your face:
NRSVCE.21:
withdraw your hand far from me,
and do not let dread of you terrify me.
NRSVCE.22:
Then call, and I will answer;
or let me speak, and you reply to me.
NRSVCE.23:
How many are my iniquities and my sins?
Make me know my transgression and my sin.
NRSVCE.24:
Why do you hide your face,
and count me as your enemy?
NRSVCE.25:
Will you frighten a windblown leaf
and pursue dry chaff?
NRSVCE.26:
For you write bitter things against me,
and make me reap the iniquities of my youth.
NRSVCE.27:
You put my feet in the stocks,
and watch all my paths;
you set a bound to the soles of my feet.
NRSVCE.28:
One wastes away like a rotten thing,
like a garment that is moth-eaten.

MSG.1:
"Yes, I've seen all this with my own eyes,
heard and understood it with my very own ears.
MSG.2:
Everything you know, I know,
so I'm not taking a back seat to any of you.
MSG.3:
I'm taking my case straight to God Almighty;
I've had it with you—I'm going directly to God.
MSG.4:
You graffiti my life with lies.
You're a bunch of pompous quacks!
MSG.5:
I wish you'd shut your mouths—
silence is your only claim to wisdom.
MSG.6:
"Listen now while I make my case,
consider my side of things for a change.
MSG.7:
Or are you going to keep on lying 'to do God a service'?
to make up stories 'to get him off the hook'?
MSG.8:
Why do you always take his side?
Do you think he needs a lawyer to defend himself?
MSG.9:
How would you fare if you were in the dock?
Your lies might convince a jury—but would they
convince God?
MSG.10:
He'd reprimand you on the spot
if he detected a bias in your witness.
MSG.11:
Doesn't his splendor put you in awe?
Aren't you afraid to speak cheap lies before him?
MSG.12:
Your wise sayings are knickknack wisdom,
good for nothing but gathering dust.
MSG.13:
"So hold your tongue while I have my say,
then I'll take whatever I have coming to me.
MSG.14:
Why do I go out on a limb like this
and take my life in my hands?
MSG.15:
Because even if he killed me, I'd keep on hoping.
I'd defend my innocence to the very end.
MSG.16:
Just wait, this is going to work out for the best—my salvation!
If I were guilt-stricken do you think I'd be doing this—
laying myself on the line before God?
MSG.17:
You'd better pay attention to what I'm telling you,
listen carefully with both ears.
MSG.18:
Now that I've laid out my defense,
I'm sure that I'll be acquitted.
MSG.19:
Can anyone prove charges against me?
I've said my piece. I rest my case.
MSG.20:
"Please, God, I have two requests;
grant them so I'll know I count with you:
MSG.21:
First, lay off the afflictions;
the terror is too much for me.
MSG.22:
Second, address me directly so I can answer you,
or let me speak and then you answer me.
MSG.23:
How many sins have been charged against me?
Show me the list—how bad is it?
MSG.24:
Why do you stay hidden and silent?
Why treat me like I'm your enemy?
MSG.25:
Why kick me around like an old tin can?
Why beat a dead horse?
MSG.26:
You compile a long list of mean things about me,
even hold me accountable for the sins of my youth.
MSG.27:
You hobble me so I can't move about.
You watch every move I make,
and brand me as a dangerous character.
MSG.28:
"Like something rotten, human life fast decomposes,
like a moth-eaten shirt or a mildewed blouse.

NET.1: “Indeed, my eyes have seen all this, my ears have heard and understood it.
NET.2: What you know, I know also; I am not inferior to you!
NET.3: But I wish to speak to the Almighty, and I desire to argue my case with God.
NET.4: But you, however, are inventors of lies; all of you are worthless physicians!
NET.5: If only you would keep completely silent! For you, that would be wisdom.
NET.6: “Listen now to my argument, and be attentive to my lips’ contentions.
NET.7: Will you speak wickedly on God’s behalf? Will you speak deceitfully for him?
NET.8: Will you show him partiality? Will you argue the case for God?
NET.9: Would it turn out well if he would examine you? Or as one deceives a man would you deceive him?
NET.10: He would certainly rebuke you if you secretly showed partiality!
NET.11: Would not his splendor terrify you and the fear he inspires fall on you?
NET.12: Your maxims are proverbs of ashes; your defenses are defenses of clay.
NET.13: “Refrain from talking with me so that I may speak; then let come to me what may.
NET.14: Why do I put myself in peril, and take my life in my hands?
NET.15: Even if he slays me, I will hope in him; I will surely defend my ways to his face!
NET.16: Moreover, this will become my deliverance, for no godless person would come before him.
NET.17: Listen carefully to my words; let your ears be attentive to my explanation.
NET.18: See now, I have prepared my case; I know that I am right.
NET.19: Who will contend with me? If anyone can, I will be silent and die.
NET.20: Only in two things spare me, O God, and then I will not hide from your face:
NET.21: Remove your hand far from me and stop making me afraid with your terror.
NET.22: Then call, and I will answer, or I will speak, and you respond to me.
NET.23: How many are my iniquities and sins? Show me my transgression and my sin.
NET.24: Why do you hide your face and regard me as your enemy?
NET.25: Do you wish to torment a windblown leaf and chase after dry chaff?
NET.26: For you write down bitter things against me and cause me to inherit the sins of my youth.
NET.27: And you put my feet in the stocks and you watch all my movements; you put marks on the soles of my feet.
NET.28: So I waste away like something rotten, like a garment eaten by moths.
